question: Article 10 of Directive 2014/24/EU excludes certain legal services – including legal representation in judicial, arbitration or conciliation proceedings and legal advice closely related to such proceedings – from its scope.

By means of Order No 3462 of 4 May 2026, the Italian Council of State (Section V) referred a number of questions for a preliminary ruling to the Court of Justice of the European Union concerning the compatibility with EU law of the Italian legislation governing the awarding of legal service contracts by public authorities.

These referrals pertain to whether the legal services referred to in Article 10 should be subject to the principles of transparency, impartiality, non-discrimination and proportionality, as well as to any obligations related to the assignment of tender identification codes and the payment of contributions to ANAC, the National Anti-Corruption Authority. In the light of the above: 1.

What is the Commission’s understanding of the interplay between Article 10 and laws that subject the services covered by the Article to the principles of transparency, impartiality, non-discrimination and proportionality?

Does the Commission think that the applicability of additional national obligations – concerning, among other things, traceability, identifiers and contributions to supervisory authorities – should also be subject to the principle of proportionality and the specific nature of the legal representation and defence services in question?
Does the Commission agree that it should promote the drafting of interpretative guidelines that ensure the uniform and proportionate application of Directive 2014/24/EU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.7.2026) The Commission acknowledges that a preliminary ruling request by a national court is pending and it can confirm that it will submit its written observations to the Court, which has the sole power to ensure the uniform interpretation of EU law across all Member States. The Commission ensures appropriate follow-up of those preliminary rulings where the Court establishes non-compliance of specific national rules under judicial scrutiny with EU law.
